plain: A researcher named Diane Powell, speaking on podcast host Jesse Michels's show in an episode about children said to read minds, talks about Kim Peek, an American man said to remember some 12,000 books. Powell says many people thought he was autistic, but that he was actually born with a defect in how his body handled cerebrospinal fluid, the liquid that cushions the brain and spine. She raises it as an example of how an unusual brain might go with unusual mental abilities.
